papers.title: What deep learning can and cannot (yet) do for enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Deep learning has substantially advanced structure-based enzyme design, yet reliably creating highly efficient enzymes remains out of reach. One emerging enzyme design strategy combines diffusion-based scaffold generation around active-site models with sequence design. Such structure-based approaches have expanded the accessible reaction space and enabled the emergence of enzymes with diverse catalytic functions and complex catalytic motifs. Despite notable catalytic efficiencies (kcat/KM), turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited, suggesting that current approaches typically yield tight sub
papers.summary: This review examines the current capabilities and limitations of deep learning for enzyme design, highlighting that while diffusion-based scaffold generation combined with sequence design has expanded accessible reaction space and produced enzymes with diverse catalytic functions, reliably achieving high catalytic efficiency remains challenging. Notably, while catalytic efficiency (kcat/KM) can be impressive, turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited, indicating that current methods typically yield tight substrate binding but not optimal catalysis.

papers.title: Molecular Evaluation of Deep Eutectic Solvents for Wet Algae Lipid Extraction and Biofuel Production.
papers.abstract: Microalgae represent promising feedstocks for biofuel production, yet cell-wall disruption remains a critical bottleneck for scaling up lipid extraction. This study evaluates four cholinium-based ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs) as green, energy-efficient pretreatment agents to facilitate the lipid release from Chlorella vulgaris under wet conditions. A geranic acid-based DES (CG 1-2 DES) was identified as the optimal agent, demonstrating direct wet biomass extraction with substantial process energy savings at comparable overall lipid yields. To minimize the energetic cost
papers.summary: This study evaluates four cholinium-based ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents as green pretreatment agents for extracting lipids from wet Chlorella vulgaris biomass, addressing the cell-wall disruption bottleneck in algal biofuel production. A geranic acid-based deep eutectic solvent (CG 1-2 DES) proved optimal, enabling direct wet biomass extraction with substantial energy savings at comparable lipid yields.

papers.title: Microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase degrades metformin to limit therapeutic response in type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Metformin is a first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes, yet therapeutic responses vary widely. Whether gut microbes directly inactivate metformin and limit its efficacy remains unclear. Here, we identify a gut microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase, AdhE, from Eubacterium species enriched in individuals with a low response to metformin. AdhE converts metformin to pharmacologically inactive products, lowering intestinal and systemic drug exposure. Genetic deletion of AdhE or phage-mediated depletion of AdhE-producing Eubacterium hallii MD1 restores metformin exposure and glycemic control in mi
papers.summary: This study identifies a gut microbial enzyme, aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase (AdhE), from Eubacterium species that converts metformin into pharmacologically inactive products, reducing drug exposure and limiting its therapeutic efficacy in type 2 diabetes. Deleting AdhE or depleting AdhE-producing E. hallii via phage restores metformin levels and improves glycemic control in mice. The findings reveal a direct microbial mechanism of drug inactivation that could explain variable patient responses to metformin.

papers.title: Genome-wide-scale prediction of compound-protein interactions using foundation and language models based on three-dimensional structures of compounds and proteins.
papers.abstract: The identification of compound-protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine-learning approach for predicting compound-protein interactions at genome-wide scale by leveraging foundation and language models that incorporate the three-dimensional structures of both compounds and proteins. The method aims to overcome the limitations of 1D and 2D representation-based models, which fail to capture geometric binding-site information critical for accurate CPI prediction. This could improve early-stage drug discovery by enabling more accurate, large-scale screening of potential compound-target pairs.

papers.title: Site-Specific Features Guiding Effective Reversible Photocontrol of Tryptophan Synthase With the Unnatural Amino Acid AzoF.
papers.abstract: This study delivers initial guidelines for the selection of effective incorporation positions for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF to facilitate the successful engineering of light-sensitive enzymes, dubbed photoxenases. Although photoxenases gain interest for the photocontrol of enzymatic activity across various fields their design has so far remained challenging. To ease particularly the selection of AzoF incorporation sites, we have systematically evaluated a total of 85 positions that differ in their biochemical and biophysical features in the bi-enzyme model system tryptopha
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates 85 different incorporation sites for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF in tryptophan synthase to identify features that enable effective reversible photocontrol of enzyme activity. The authors provide initial guidelines for selecting positions that yield light-sensitive 'photoxenases', addressing a key challenge in engineering photocontrolled enzymes.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors introduce MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to predict enzyme turnover numbers (kcat) by jointly modeling enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints. They also built MCKcat-DB, a large dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat measurements, and demonstrate its utility for rational enzyme evolution. This addresses a key bottleneck in biocatalysis where experimental kcat determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods poorly capture enzyme-reaction interplay.

papers.title: GPCR heteromers: Beyond the monomeric paradigm in neuropsychiatric drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest druggable superfamily of membrane proteins and underlie approximately 35% of all approved medicines. Yet this conventional paradigm leaves a substantial minority of neuropsychiatric patients with incomplete efficacy, treatment resistance, or dose-limiting adverse effects. Converging evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and molecular pharmacology has dismantled the monomeric model. GPCRs function in vivo as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes in brain regions directly implicated in disease, including the
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review argues that GPCRs operate in the brain as dynamic homo- and heteromeric complexes rather than as isolated monomers, challenging the classical drug-discovery paradigm that targets single receptors. The authors synthesize structural, biophysical, and pharmacological evidence showing these heteromers are relevant to neuropsychiatric disease and may explain incomplete treatment responses. They propose that targeting GPCR heteromers could open new therapeutic avenues for patients with treatment-resistant conditions.

papers.title: A de novo GABPA Variant in a Patient with Multifocal Cutaneous Vascular Tumors of an Unclassified Entity.
papers.abstract: We investigated the genetic basis of a previously unclassified congenital vascular anomaly in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors. Through genomic analysis, we identified a novel heterozygous de novo germline variant in GA-binding protein-alpha (GABPA), an ETS family transcription factor. Histopathologic evaluation demonstrated capillary-venous lesions lacking glucose transporter 1 expression, distinguishing this entity from common infantile hemangioma. Notably, the tumor vasculature exhibited a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular cell layer, with nuclear localized GABPA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This case study identifies a novel de novo germline variant in the GABPA transcription factor in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors that do not fit any previously classified entity. The tumors show distinct histopathology, including GLUT1-negative capillary-venous lesions and a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular layer, suggesting GABPA dysfunction drives this unclassified vascular anomaly.

papers.title: Criteria-guided selection of alternative zinc-binding groups of HDAC3 inhibitors using in silico and in vitro approaches.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are epigenetic enzymes linked to several biological functions and diseases. Class I HDACs (HDAC1-3) share high protein sequence and active site similarity. Hydroxamate-based inhibitors, while highly potent, are non-selective with poor pharmacokinetic profile, prompting exploration of alternative zinc-binding groups. The study applied criteria-guided identification of HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups following structure-based virtual screening, with a prioritisation of HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate interaction wit
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening followed by in vitro testing to identify HDAC3 inhibitors bearing alternative zinc-binding groups, aiming to overcome the poor selectivity and pharmacokinetic issues of traditional hydroxamate inhibitors. The authors prioritized compounds forming HDAC3-specific interactions and bidentate/monodentate zinc coordination, yielding candidate inhibitors with potentially improved profiles.

papers.title: [Rational design for improving the thermostability of β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans].
papers.abstract: The β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans (Bgl52) has been identified as a thermophilic and acidophilic β-glucosidase, which constitutes the most critical component in the cellulolytic enzyme system for cellulose hydrolysis. Although Bgl52 is a thermophilic enzyme, its poor thermal stability at high temperatures restricts its long-term industrial application under elevated-temperature conditions. In this study, rational design strategies, including two free energy calculation programs (Fireprot and FoldX) and homologous sequence alignment, were integrated to perform single-point and mu
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study applies rational design strategies—including the free energy calculation tools Fireprot and FoldX plus homologous sequence alignment—to engineer the thermophilic β-glucosidase Bgl52 from Bacillus thermoamylovorans for improved thermal stability. The goal is to overcome the enzyme's poor stability at high temperatures, which currently limits its long-term industrial use in cellulose hydrolysis.

papers.title: Site-specific phosphorylation of Ser352 drives aggregation of Tau R4 under acidosis conditions.
papers.abstract: In Alzheimer's disease, neurons undergo acidosis as their pH drops from ∼7.1 to ∼6.5. Here we elucidate the molecular mechanism of specific Tau aggregation only at this lower pH. We show that a specific phosphorylation event in the Tau R4 domain is coupled to this pH drop to drive a defined phase transition from condensates to fibrils. Using a combination of experimental and computational studies, our results demonstrate that site-specific phosphorylation of Ser352 is the molecular switch that induces aggregation of Tau only at the more acidic, disease-related pH. We designed and synthesized a
papers.summary: This study identifies phosphorylation of Ser352 in the Tau R4 domain as a molecular switch that triggers Tau aggregation specifically under the acidic conditions (pH ~6.5) found in Alzheimer's disease neurons. Combining experimental and computational approaches, the authors show this site-specific modification drives a phase transition from liquid condensates to fibrils only at disease-relevant pH. The work provides a mechanistic link between neuronal acidosis and Tau pathology.

papers.title: A water-pinning hotspot drives templated tau aggregation.
papers.abstract: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP), achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured sol
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how the intrinsically disordered protein tau achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils, proposing that a single dominant 'water-pinning' hotspot mediates tau-tau and tau-seed interactions to prevent mismatched stacking. The findings suggest a templated aggregation mechanism relevant to the prion-like spread of tauopathies.

papers.title: DesignMaster: A Multi-Conditional Diffusion Framework for Rational PROTAC Design.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation through ternary complex formation with E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, the rational design of PROTACs remains highly challenging due to limited structure-activity relationship data and the vast conformational diversity of linkers. Existing computational approaches can be broadly divided into structure-based ternary modelling methods and fragment-based linker generation models. Although these approaches have advanced PROTAC design, they typically neglect key physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during th
papers.summary: DesignMaster introduces a multi-conditional diffusion framework for rationally designing PROTAC molecules, which are bifunctional compounds that degrade target proteins via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Unlike prior structure-based or fragment-based methods, it incorporates physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during generation, addressing a key gap in computational PROTAC design.

papers.title: Targeting DYRK1A with rationally designed pyrazine-guanidine hybrids for Alzheimer's disease: design, synthesis, and biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: Dual-specificity tyrosine phosphorylation-regulated kinase 1A (DYRK1A) has been implicated in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) by regulating tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammatory pathways, suggesting DYRK1A as an important therapeutic target. Herein, we report the rational design, synthesis and evaluation of a new class of low-molecular-weight pyrazine-guanidine molecular hybrids as potential DYRK1A inhibitors via an integrated computational and experimental approach. Molecular docking studies predicted good protein-ligand interactions, with compounds F1, F5, and F7 exhibi
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of novel pyrazine-guanidine hybrid molecules intended to inhibit DYRK1A, a kinase implicated in Alzheimer's disease through tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammation. Using molecular docking followed by experimental evaluation, compounds F1, F5, and F7 showed promising protein-ligand interactions, suggesting these hybrids could serve as lead candidates for DYRK1A-targeted AD therapy.

papers.title: Sulfur source-driven global remodeling of gene expression in the fuel-biodesulfurizing Rhodococcus qingshengii IGTS8.
papers.abstract: Recent proteomics and metabolomics studies have confirmed the significance of understanding the fuel biodesulfurization phenotype at a global scale beyond the desulfurization 4S pathway. To reveal the transcriptomic adaptations in the model strain Rhodococcus qingshengii IGTS8 under biodesulfurization conditions, we conducted a time series comparative RNA-seq study using cultures of IGTS8 grown on either dibenzothiophene (DBT) or MgSO4 as the sulfur source. The RNA-seq data revealed many differentially expressed genes (DEGs) depending on the sulfur source and growth phase, and the strongest tr
papers.summary: This study used time-series RNA-seq to compare the transcriptome of Rhodococcus qingshengii IGTS8 grown with dibenzothiophene versus MgSO4 as sulfur sources, revealing extensive sulfur-source-dependent gene expression changes across growth phases. The findings show that biodesulfurization involves global remodeling of gene expression beyond the known 4S desulfurization pathway, highlighting broader metabolic adaptations.

papers.title: Evolutionary Dynamics-Aware De Novo Design of a Thermostable NS1-Derived Diagnostic Protein for Yellow Fever Virus.
papers.abstract: Serological diagnosis of neglected arboviruses remains hindered by extensive intra-genus cross-reactivity, compromising both assay specificity and epidemiological accuracy. In this study, we focused on yellow fever virus (YFV) as a model system to design and validate a generalizable de novo protein design framework integrating evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to rationally engineer diagnostic antigens with reduced cross-reactivity and improved cost-effectiveness. Through comprehensive evolutionary mapping over time of the YFV polyprotein, we identified conserved yet discriminator
papers.summary: The authors developed a de novo protein design framework that combines evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to engineer a thermostable diagnostic antigen derived from the yellow fever virus NS1 protein. By mapping evolutionary conservation across the YFV polyprotein, they identified regions that are conserved but antigenically discriminating, aiming to reduce cross-reactivity with related flaviviruses in serological assays. The resulting designed protein is intended to improve specificity and cost-effectiveness of YFV diagnostics.

papers.title: Mechanism-Driven Design of Metal-Phenolic Networks: From Precision Assembly to Multidimensional Synergistic Therapy for Brain Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background: Brain disorders, such as glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease and ischemic stroke, represent formidable challenges due to the highly restrictive blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the complex pathophysiological microenvironment, which severely compromise drug delivery and therapeutic outcomes. Metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), as a class of novel hybrid materials, hold great promise for overcoming brain delivery bottlenecks and enabling precise synergistic therapy by leveraging their unique physicochemical properties. However, a comprehensive synthesis of MPN designs tailored specifically to
papers.summary: This review discusses metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), a class of hybrid materials, as a strategy for overcoming the blood-brain barrier and treating brain diseases like glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease, and ischemic stroke. It synthesizes design principles for MPNs, from precision assembly to multidimensional synergistic therapy, highlighting their potential for improved brain drug delivery.

papers.title: Pockets to products: a data-driven approach for classification of monoterpene synthases.
papers.abstract: Monoterpene synthases (mTSs) are a large family of enzymes, which have promising industrial applications, yet remain difficult to engineer due to complex and poorly understood sequence-function relationships. Here, we present a structure-based machine learning (ML) framework that accurately predicts whether a mTS is likely to produce linalool or limonene, chosen as canonical examples of linear and cyclic monoterpene products, respectively. Our approach identifies active site properties, which are used as ML features, enabling functional predictions that go beyond sequence alone. As residue pos
papers.summary: This paper presents a structure-based machine learning framework that predicts whether a monoterpene synthase (mTS) enzyme will produce linalool (linear) or limonene (cyclic). By using active site properties as features rather than sequence alone, the approach captures functional determinants that sequence-based methods miss. This offers a data-driven route to guide engineering of these industrially valuable enzymes.

papers.title: Morphology Evolution and Structural Reorganization of Enzyme-Biosurfactant Systems: Implications for Petroleum Interfacial Engineering.
papers.abstract: The escalating demand for sustainable chemical solutions in petroleum engineering has catalyzed the development of bio-based formulations characterized by high interfacial activity and low environmental toxicity. This study investigates the intermolecular interactions and structural evolution within composite systems comprising representative glycolipid biosurfactants and carbohydrate hydrolases. Rheological and light scattering assessments reveal that the introduction of enzymes triggers a transition from large-scale micelles to highly dispersed micro-aggregates, accompanied by a significant
papers.summary: This study examines how adding carbohydrate hydrolase enzymes to glycolipid biosurfactants changes the system's structure, causing a shift from large micelles to smaller, dispersed micro-aggregates. The findings suggest these enzyme-biosurfactant mixtures could improve interfacial performance in petroleum engineering applications.

papers.title: High-throughput physics-based enzyme engineering.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering aims to tailor natural enzymes for industrial and therapeutic applications, yet physically grounded rational design has been limited by a trade-off between accuracy and cost, leaving the field heavily dependent on expert intuition. Here we present a scalable physics-based framework that combines field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to capture enzyme electrostatics at quantum-mechanical accuracy while enabling efficient, atomistic exploration of reaction free-energy landscapes. Coupled with microkinetic modelling, the framework translates molecular free-energ
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a scalable enzyme engineering framework that combines field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to model enzyme electrostatics at quantum-mechanical accuracy while remaining computationally efficient. Coupled with microkinetic modeling, it enables high-throughput exploration of reaction free-energy landscapes to guide rational enzyme design without relying on expert intuition.

papers.title: Engineered mRNA nanostructures expand the design space of mRNA therapeutics through programmable protein expression and immune stimulation.
papers.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have transformed vaccination and protein replacement strategies, yet efforts to improve their performance have focused largely on sequence engineering, nucleotide modification, and delivery vehicles. Here we show that mRNA function can be controlled by rational design of higher-order RNA architectures. We develop self-assembling mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of unimolecular RNA nanostructures that encode protein-coding sequences within higher-order, programmable, and compact nucleic acid architectures. Using computational design and experimental validation,
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of self-assembling, unimolecular RNA nanostructures that embed protein-coding sequences within programmable higher-order architectures. The authors use computational design and experimental validation to show that these engineered mRNA structures can tune protein expression and stimulate immune responses, expanding the design space beyond sequence optimization and delivery vehicles.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: KAN-GIN replaces the standard multilayer perceptron in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation to improve drug-target affinity prediction. The framework combines molecular graph representations with a convolutional protein sequence encoder and was benchmarked on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ against a matched GIN baseline. Results suggest that adaptive nonlinear transformations can modestly enhance affinity prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates the current state of molecular docking studies on natural products, highlighting the wide variability in methodological quality and the lack of standardized guidelines. It examines how different natural-product classes and protein targets require tailored docking approaches, and offers practical recommendations to improve rigor and reproducibility in the field.

papers.title: Unveiling Novel Metalloprotease Inhibitors Targeting Botulinum Neurotoxin Through Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Drug Libraries and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) is one of the most lethal biological substances to humans, which inhibits acetylcholine release by the presynaptic nerve in neuromuscular junctions. Of the existing BoNT serotypes, BoNT serotype A (BoNT/A) is particularly potent, making it the primary focus in neurotoxin research. Its catalytic domain exhibits similar structural features and zinc-dependent activity as thermolysin, a key bacterial enzyme, which provides a foundation for designing antibacterial agents targeting related protease mechanisms. Repurposing of preapproved drugs or existing medications has r
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening of existing drug libraries combined with molecular dynamics simulations to identify novel metalloprotease inhibitors targeting the catalytic domain of botulinum neurotoxin serotype A. The approach leverages the structural similarity between BoNT/A and thermolysin to repurpose preapproved drugs as potential therapeutics against this highly lethal neurotoxin.

papers.title: Dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-ones and Benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-ones: Useful Scaffolds for Development of Protein-Protein Interaction Inhibitors †.
papers.abstract: Modulation of protein-protein interactions (PPIs) by small molecules is a vital strategy in drug discovery. Nevertheless, due to the inherent nature of PPI interfaces, practical implementation of this approach remains a high-hanging fruit in medicinal chemistry. In this report, we develop a new line of PEX14-PEX5 PPI inhibitors by homologation of a previously developed dibenzo[b,e]azepin-6(6H)-one scaffold. The challenging chemistry of 8-membered ring formation led to the development of novel PEX14 inhibitors featuring a 6+8+6 tricyclic system. The obtained analogs were tested for their capabi
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis of novel dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-one and benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-one scaffolds, which are 8-membered ring tricyclic systems, as inhibitors of the PEX14-PEX5 protein-protein interaction. The authors homologated a previously developed dibenzo[b,e]azepin-6(6H)-one scaffold to create these new compounds and evaluated their inhibitory activity. The work provides new chemical scaffolds for developing PPI inhibitors, a challenging area in drug discovery.

papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts secreted effector proteins in Gram-negative bacteria by combining protein language model sequence embeddings with geometric features derived from predicted 3D structures. This structure-aware approach aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only methods and the scarcity of experimental structures, improving effector identification for understanding bacterial pathogenesis.

papers.title: Fast structural search for classification of gut bacterial mucin O-glycan degrading enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering scheme provides a hierarchical way to classify enzymes according to their catalytic functions. While recent protein language model (PLM) based approaches like CLEAN and ProteInter have improved sequence-based EC number prediction, they struggle with fine-grained classification at the deepest hierarchical level. Structure-based approaches for grouping similar proteins using alignment tools excel at finding proteins that share overall global structure, but suffer from high false positive rates when classifying proteins that are globally structurally similar b
papers.summary: The authors present a fast structural search method for classifying gut bacterial enzymes that degrade mucin O-glycans, addressing the difficulty of fine-grained EC number prediction at the deepest hierarchical level. Their approach improves on sequence-based protein language model methods like CLEAN and ProteInter, which struggle with closely related enzyme functions, and on alignment-based structural tools that produce high false positive rates for globally similar proteins.

papers.title: Evaluation of 6-substituted coumarins as SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors: enzymatic, cellular, and computational insights.
papers.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) plays a crucial role in viral replication, making it an attractive target for antiviral drug development. This study evaluates the inhibitory potential of nineteen 6-substituted coumarin derivatives (1a-p and 2a-c) against Mpro using a FRET-based enzymatic assay. Among them, the chlorinated derivative 1f (AKE-9306) exhibited the highest potency with an IC50 value of 61.77 µM. Enzyme kinetics analysis through Michaelis-Menten and Lineweaver-Burk plots revealed that compound 1f may act through a mixed-type inhibition mechanism with a preference for the free en
papers.summary: This study screened nineteen 6-substituted coumarin derivatives for their ability to inhibit the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro), a key enzyme in viral replication. The chlorinated compound 1f (AKE-9306) was the most potent inhibitor with an IC50 of 61.77 µM, and kinetic analysis suggested a mixed-type inhibition mechanism. The findings provide a starting point for further optimization of coumarin-based Mpro inhibitors.

papers.title: Simulating Infrared Spectra of Matrix Isolation Experiments: What Works Best?
papers.abstract: Matrix isolation is an experimental technique which allows spectroscopists to observe highly reactive or weakly bound systems by trapping them in frozen noble gas matrices. In this work, we studied the viability of using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to simulate several H2S·amine complexes isolated in solid argon crystals, comparing the results with conventional density functional theory (DFT) harmonic and anharmonic calculations to assess the most practical and accurate method to calculate the vibrational spectrum of such systems. While AIMD accurately predicted the intensity ratios of
papers.summary: This study compares ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) against conventional harmonic and anharmonic DFT calculations for simulating infrared spectra of H2S·amine complexes trapped in solid argon matrices. AIMD accurately reproduced intensity ratios, suggesting it is a viable approach for modeling matrix isolation spectra, though trade-offs in cost and accuracy are discussed.

papers.title: Characterization of MdDOX-Co homologs revealed a novel gibberellin metabolic clade and a single-residue switch dictating the catalytic site.
papers.abstract: The metabolism of gibberellin (GA) is generally mediated by GA 2-oxidase (GA2ox) through 2β-hydroxylation. These enzymes belong to the 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase (2ODD, DOX) superfamily. However, MdDOX-Co, another 2ODD, was recently found to catalyze atypical GA 12α-hydroxylation. MdDOX-Co belongs to the DOXC41 clade, which is phylogenetically distant from the canonical GA2ox. The evolutionary and structural bases of this unique catalytic site remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the functional divergence of the DOXC41 clade. Through phylogenetic analyses, biochemical exper
papers.summary: This study characterizes MdDOX-Co homologs and identifies a novel gibberellin metabolic clade (DOXC41) that is evolutionarily distinct from canonical GA2ox enzymes. The authors pinpoint a single amino acid residue that acts as a switch determining whether the enzyme performs typical 2β-hydroxylation or atypical 12α-hydroxylation. This provides structural and evolutionary insight into how catalytic specificity diverged within the 2ODD superfamily.

papers.title: Ophiopogonin D suppresses non-small cell lung cancer progression by targeting exosomal MALAT1 to enhance dendritic cell maturation.
papers.abstract: Tumor-immune cell crosstalk critically shapes the progression of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the mechanisms underlying exosome-mediated immune suppression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized exosomal lncRNA-mediated immunoregulatory axis targeted by the natural compound Ophiopogonin D (OP-D). Transcriptomic profiling and mechanistic rescue experiments revealed that Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC)-derived exosomal MALAT1 suppresses dendritic cell (DC) maturation by increasing SIRT1 expression and attenuating p65 phosphorylation. Computational model
papers.summary: This study identifies a new mechanism by which lung cancer cells suppress the immune system: exosomes carrying the lncRNA MALAT1 inhibit dendritic cell maturation by boosting SIRT1 and reducing p65 phosphorylation. The natural compound Ophiopogonin D blocks this pathway, restoring dendritic cell maturation and slowing non-small cell lung cancer progression, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Discovery and Biological Characterization of 1-[4-(2-Difluoromethoxyphenyl)-5-methylthiazol-2-yl]-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)urea (DFMNTU): A Novel Thiazolyl-Urea Chemotype Targeting Yellow Fever Virus and Host Casein Kinase 2 (CK2).
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a re- emerging mosquito- borne flavivirus that causes severe hemorrhagic fever with high case- fatality rates. Due to vaccine contraindications, incomplete immunization coverage, and the absence of approved specific antivirals, host- directed drug discovery targeting cellular machinery exploited by YFV is a critical therapeutic priority. Here, 1-[4-(2- difluoromethoxyphenyl)- 5- methylthiazol- 2- yl]- 3-(naphthalen- 1- yl)urea (DFMNTU) was synthesized, characterized by NMR, MS, and HPLC, and evaluated for antiviral efficacy against YFV strain 17 D in Vero cells. DFM
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of DFMNTU, a novel thiazolyl-urea compound that targets yellow fever virus by inhibiting the host protein casein kinase 2 (CK2). The compound shows antiviral activity against YFV strain 17D in cell culture, suggesting host-directed antiviral strategies could be effective against this re-emerging flavivirus.

papers.title: Comprehensive insights into thermodynamic stability, optoelectronic properties, thermoelectric properties, and photocatalytic hydrogen evolution potential of halide double perovskites Rb2TlAlX6 (X = Cl, Br, I): first-principles and AIMD approach.
papers.abstract: Rubidium (Rb)-based halide double perovskites (HDPs) possessing tunable optoelectronic features have emerged as promising substances for optoelectronic, thermoelectric, and photocatalytic hydrogen production technologies. In the present work, Rb2TlAlX6 (X = Cl, Br, and I) HDPs are reported using a first-principles approach. The optimized lattice parameters, tolerance factors, and formation energy validate the cubic phase and thermal integrity of the studied HDPs at 300 K. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulation confirms thermal stability at 300 K, and phonon spectra validate dynamic sta
papers.summary: This study uses first-principles calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics to characterize the structural, thermodynamic, optoelectronic, and thermoelectric properties of Rb2TlAlX6 halide double perovskites (X = Cl, Br, I), and evaluates their potential for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. The authors report that these materials form stable cubic phases with tunable properties, suggesting promise for optoelectronic and thermoelectric applications.

papers.title: Neuroprotective eremophilane sesquiterpenoids from Ligularia species attenuate glutamate-induced oxidative stress via MAPK signaling.
papers.abstract: Ligularia species (Asteraceae) have long been used in traditional East Asian medicine for the treatment of pain and inflammatory disorders. Although neuroprotection is not among their documented traditional indications, the close relationship among inflammation, oxidative stress, and neuronal injury, together with the reported analgesic and anti-inflammatory activities of these species, provides a rationale for investigating their neuroprotective potential.
papers.summary: This study investigates eremophilane sesquiterpenoids isolated from Ligularia species for neuroprotective activity, testing whether they can protect neurons from glutamate-induced oxidative stress. The authors link the observed protection to modulation of MAPK signaling pathways, providing a mechanistic basis for a neuroprotective effect not previously documented in traditional use.

papers.title: Venom-derived and natural analgesic peptides: From venomics-based discovery to computational design and therapeutic development.
papers.abstract: Pain is a complex physiological process and an important clinical issue due to thelimitations of the existing analgesics. Side effects, tolerance anddependence, and limited efficacy for the treatment of chronic pain are common complications of classic drugs, e.g., opioids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). In the last decade, analgesic peptides have gained considerable attention as new drug candidates due to their high target specificity, structural complexity, and ability to interact with critical molecular players of nociceptive signaling such as ion channels, receptors and i
papers.summary: This review examines venom-derived and natural peptides as promising alternatives to conventional analgesics like opioids and NSAIDs, which suffer from side effects, tolerance, and limited chronic pain efficacy. It covers the pipeline from venomics-based discovery through computational design to therapeutic development, highlighting how these peptides target key nociceptive signaling molecules such as ion channels and receptors.

papers.title: Origin-specific metabolomic profiling and network pharmacology propose potential multi-target antioxidant mechanisms of black sesame seeds.
papers.abstract: Black Sesame Seeds (BSS) are consumed as an edible herbal food with medicinal food homology and possess potent antioxidant properties; however, their metabolic compositions and corresponding antioxidant efficacies substantially vary across different geographical origins. This study investigates the underlying multi-component and multi-target antioxidant mechanisms of BSS from various geographical origins. An integrated computational and experimental approach combining UHPLC-Q-Exactive Orbitrap MS/MS-based metabolomics, network pharmacology, and molecular docking was employed. Metabolomic profi
papers.summary: This study combined UHPLC-Q-Exactive Orbitrap MS/MS metabolomics with network pharmacology and molecular docking to profile black sesame seeds from different geographical origins. The authors identified origin-specific metabolite differences and proposed multi-target antioxidant mechanisms, linking specific compounds to antioxidant activity. The work highlights how geographic origin influences the medicinal food properties of black sesame seeds.

papers.title: Elucidating the MultiPathway Therapeutic Potential of Trichosantheskirilowii Bioactives in Intestinal Obstruction via Network Pharmacology and Molecular Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Intestinal obstruction (IO) disrupts normal intestinal transit and involves dysmotility, mucosal stress, and inflammation. This computational workflow evaluated a 10-compound Trichosanthes kirilowii docking panel, a filtered disease-target set, MOE docking validation, and 100 ns MOE molecular dynamics and MM/GBSA endpoint analyses. GeneCards filtering (relevance >= 10) and OMIM curation yielded a primary disease union of 756 genes; 31 targets overlapped with a broadened 203-target herb-associated set, and the overlap was significant by hypergeometric testing (p = 6.38 × 10-11). Docking across
papers.summary: This computational study uses network pharmacology, molecular docking, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations to explore how ten bioactive compounds from Trichosanthes kirilowii might act against intestinal obstruction. The authors identified 31 overlapping targets between the herb's compound set and disease-associated genes, with significant enrichment, and used docking plus MM/GBSA analyses to prioritize likely compound-target interactions. The work proposes multi-pathway therapeutic mechanisms but remains entirely in silico without experimental validation.

papers.title: A Multi-Scale Computational Framework for Anti-Persister Tuberculosis Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Latent tuberculosis (TB), caused by dormant, non-replicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), afflicts an estimated 1.7 billion individuals globally and remains a principal barrier to TB eradication. Dormant bacilli are phenotypically tolerant to conventional antibiotics and survive through continued dependence on oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and the electron transport chain (ETC), making bioenergetic enzymes, including the F1Fo-ATP synthase, cytochrome bcc:aa3 supercomplex, Type II NADH dehydrogenase (NDH-2) and cytochrome bd oxidase, compelling drug targets. This review proposes and r
papers.summary: This review proposes a multi-scale computational framework for discovering drugs that target dormant, drug-tolerant Mycobacterium tuberculosis persisters, which cause latent TB in roughly 1.7 billion people. It highlights bioenergetic enzymes—F1Fo-ATP synthase, cytochrome bcc:aa3 supercomplex, NDH-2, and cytochrome bd oxidase—as promising targets because dormant bacilli remain dependent on oxidative phosphorylation and the electron transport chain.

papers.title: Unraveling insights for ion transport enhancement by metal-organic framework-5 in polyethylene oxide and polyvinylidene fluoride electrolytes: classical molecular dynamics and metadynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The structural and dynamical properties of simulation systems consisting of metal organic frameworks (MOFs), particularly MOF-5, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) salt, and two well-known polymers, poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO), in different compositions were investigated using classical molecular dynamics (cMD) and well-tempered metadynamics (WT-MD) simulations. The cMD simulations revealed that the PEO-based hybrid electrolyte system containing LiTFSI salt and MOF-5 (System D) exhibits the highest diffusion coefficient for Li+ ions and comp
papers.summary: This study uses classical molecular dynamics and well-tempered metadynamics simulations to investigate how MOF-5 affects lithium ion transport in polymer electrolytes based on PEO and PVDF with LiTFSI salt. The PEO-based hybrid system containing MOF-5 showed the highest Li+ diffusion coefficient, suggesting MOF-5 can enhance ion transport in solid polymer electrolytes for battery applications.

papers.title: Trypsinogen Pro-Region as a Molecular Scaffold for the Design of Competitive Peptide Inhibitors of Trypsin-Like Proteases.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. Merrill) productivity is severely impacted by the velvetbean caterpillar Anticarsia gemmatalis Hübner, 1818 (Lepidoptera: Erebidae), a major defoliating pest in soybean-producing regions. Current management strategies rely heavily on chemical insecticides, which are associated with environmental risks and the development of resistance. Protease inhibitors have emerged as a promising alternative, as protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae is primarily mediated by trypsin-like serine proteases. In this context, the rational design of short inhibitory peptides represents
papers.journal: Archives of insect biochemistry and physiology
papers.summary: The paper explores using the pro-region of trypsinogen as a molecular scaffold to rationally design short competitive peptide inhibitors targeting trypsin-like serine proteases in the velvetbean caterpillar, a major soybean pest. This approach aims to provide an environmentally friendly alternative to chemical insecticides by disrupting protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae.

papers.title: Multidimensional molecular profiling reveals decidual and circulating NK cell dynamics in early and late pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Human pregnancy presents a unique physiological state that allows for growth of an antigenically dissimilar foetus. The immune system plays a key role in establishing and maintaining successful pregnancy, yet detailed understanding of immunological responses in pregnancy is lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses multidimensional molecular profiling to characterize natural killer (NK) cell populations in both the decidua (uterine lining) and peripheral blood across early and late pregnancy. It reveals dynamic changes in NK cell composition and phenotype that likely support maternal immune tolerance of the fetus. The findings provide a detailed immune atlas of pregnancy that could inform understanding of pregnancy complications.

papers.title: Discovery of dietary polyphenols targeting the autoinducer-2 quorum sensing system of pathogenic bacteria.
papers.abstract: Targeting autoinducer-2 (AI-2) quorum sensing (QS) systems with dietary compounds represents a promising strategy to combat pathogens, yet mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we develop a machine learning-driven framework combining computational screening with multi-level experimental analysis to identify AI-2 quorum sensing interference molecules (QSIMs). A graph neural network (GNN)-based classifier (AI2IMpred) screens over 7000 phytochemicals and identifies dietary polyphenols as potent QSIMs. Using Salmonella Typhimurium LT2 as a model, we demonstrate that 17 polyphenols, including pterostilb
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning framework (AI2IMpred), based on a graph neural network, to screen over 7000 phytochemicals for molecules that interfere with the autoinducer-2 (AI-2) quorum sensing system of pathogenic bacteria. The screen identifies dietary polyphenols as potent quorum sensing interference molecules (QSIMs), with 17 polyphenols validated experimentally in Salmonella Typhimurium LT2. The work highlights dietary polyphenols as promising candidates for disrupting bacterial communication and combating pathogens.

papers.title: Evolutionary and structural pathways of antibody maturation reveal principles for engineering potent SARS-CoV-2 neutralizers.
papers.abstract: The continual emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants underscores the need to elucidate antibody maturation and apply rational design principles to optimize therapeutics. This study focused on vaccine-elicited 9C lineage, encoded by IGHV4-34, as a model for affinity maturation and structural refinement. Sequence analyses revealed strong framework conservation alongside focused diversification within CDRH3, where the invariant RWFD anchor and a recurrent SYTV block were consistently associated with potent neutralization. Phylogenetic reconstruction traced a trajectory from weakly neutralizing precurso
papers.summary: This study traces how a vaccine-elicited antibody lineage (9C, using IGHV4-34) matures to potently neutralize SARS-CoV-2, showing that the framework stays conserved while diversification concentrates in CDRH3. Specific motifs—an invariant RWFD anchor and a recurrent SYTV block—are consistently linked to strong neutralization, and phylogenetic reconstruction maps the path from weak precursors to potent variants. These principles could guide rational engineering of improved antibody therapeutics.

papers.title: Effects of lawsone and lawsone methyl ether on cyclooxygenase activity, redox balance, and organ-specific toxicity: An integrated computational and experimental study.
papers.abstract: Redox imbalance contributes significantly to the initiation and progression of inflammatory responses. Although conventional anti-inflammatory drugs are widely used, their prolonged administration is associated with a number of adverse effects. Lawsone methyl ether (LME) and lawsone are plant-derived, redox-active naphthoquinones, exhibiting diverse pharmacological activities; however, their cyclooxygenase (COX)-inhibitory effects, redox-modulatory properties, and oral toxicity profiles remain insufficiently characterized. Therefore, this study investigated the COX-inhibitory activity, redox-m
papers.summary: This study evaluates two plant-derived naphthoquinones, lawsone and lawsone methyl ether, for their ability to inhibit cyclooxygenase enzymes and modulate redox balance, using combined computational and experimental approaches. It also assesses organ-specific toxicity to gauge their safety as potential alternatives to conventional anti-inflammatory drugs. The findings characterize their COX-inhibitory and redox-modulatory properties alongside oral toxicity profiles.

papers.title: Identification of Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 with potential relevance to prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Glutathione S-transferase Pi 1 (GSTP1) is frequently silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD), yet whether its residual catalytic activity can be chemically enhanced is largely unexplored. Here, we identify Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 through structure-based screening, biophysical characterisation, and biochemical validation. Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) supported a concentration-dependent association between Crocin I and GSTP1, and enzymatic assays demonstrated enhanced catalytic activity. Michaelis-Menten kinetics showed that Crocin I increased Vmax without markedly alterin
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study identifies Crocin I, a natural compound, as a positive modulator that binds to and enhances the catalytic activity of GSTP1, an enzyme often silenced in prostate cancer. Using structure-based screening, biophysical binding assays, and enzyme kinetics, the authors show Crocin I increases GSTP1 activity, suggesting a potential chemical strategy to boost residual GSTP1 function in prostate adenocarcinoma.

papers.title: Shenling Qige Granules inhibit esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression in TE-1 xenograft and cell-based models by modulating the DCN-TGF-β/Smad signaling axis.
papers.abstract: Shenling Qige Granules (SLQG), derived from the Qing Dynasty formula Qige San recorded in Yi Xue Xin Wu, has been used in clinical practice in China as an adjuvant traditional Chinese medicine preparation for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but its molecular basis remains unclear. This study investigated the antitumor effects and mechanisms of SLQG using TE-1 xenograft mice and SLQG-containing serum-treated TE-1 cells. Transcriptome sequencing, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and public-database analysis were integrated to prioritize candidate
papers.summary: This study investigates how a traditional Chinese medicine formula, Shenling Qige Granules (SLQG), inhibits esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) growth. Using mouse xenograft models and TE-1 cancer cells, combined with transcriptomics, network pharmacology, and molecular docking, the authors identify the DCN-TGF-β/Smad signaling axis as a key pathway through which SLQG exerts its antitumor effects.

papers.title: Preclinical identification of an oxadiazole-pyrazole lead targeting prostate cancer through integrated mechanistic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among men, while resistance to androgen deprivation therapy emphasizes the need for new therapeutic strategies. Molecular hybridization of pharmacologically relevant heterocycles offers a rational approach for developing novel anticancer agents.
papers.summary: This study reports the preclinical identification of a novel oxadiazole-pyrazole hybrid compound as a lead candidate for prostate cancer therapy. The authors used integrated mechanistic evaluations to characterize its anticancer activity, addressing the need for new treatments in the context of androgen deprivation therapy resistance. The work highlights molecular hybridization of heterocycles as a rational drug design strategy.

papers.title: Integrated AUF-UPLC-MS and fraction-activity correlation to identify COX-2-targeted constituents of Shaoyao Gancao decoction.
papers.abstract: Shaoyao Gancao Decoction (SGD), a classical multi-ingredient herbal formula, exerts potent anti-inflammatory and anti-rheumatoid arthritis effects against rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Existing cellular experiments have proven that SGD can downregulate Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression in inflammatory macrophages, implying a potential link between its anti-arthritic efficacy and COX-2 modulation. Nevertheless, its constituents with potential COX-2 binding capacity and corresponding anti-RA material basis are unclear, hindering its pharmaceutical exploitation. In this study, an integrated strate
papers.summary: This study combines affinity ultrafiltration with UPLC-MS and fraction-activity correlation to identify which chemical constituents of Shaoyao Gancao Decoction bind to and potentially inhibit COX-2, an inflammation-related enzyme. The approach links specific herbal compounds to anti-inflammatory activity, helping clarify the material basis of this traditional formula's anti-rheumatoid arthritis effects.

papers.title: Mitochondria affect antibacterial immunity in cross talk with innate immune response molecules coded by genes of nuclear origin.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria are dynamic, semi-autonomous organelles that, in addition to their central role in ATP production, regulate calcium homeostasis, iron metabolism, apoptosis, and innate immune signalling. Although the mitochondrial genome encodes only 37 genes, mitochondrial architecture, bioenergetic function, and dynamics are governed predominantly by nuclear-encoded proteins, necessitating highly coordinated communication between mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and the nuclear genome. Disruption of this bidirectional mitochondrial-nuclear crosstalk has been increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis
papers.summary: This review examines how mitochondria, largely controlled by nuclear-encoded proteins, influence antibacterial innate immunity through bidirectional mitochondrial-nuclear crosstalk. It highlights how disruption of this communication contributes to immune dysfunction and pathogenesis, integrating mitochondrial dynamics, bioenergetics, and mtDNA signaling with host defense.

papers.title: BDE-47 and male infertility: integrated network toxicology, single-cell transcriptomics, and in vitro evidence of GSTM1 downregulation and ferroptosis-related molecular remodeling in Leydig cells.
papers.abstract: BDE-47 is a widely detected polybrominated diphenyl ether with potential male reproductive toxicity, but the key testicular cell populations and molecular basis remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the environmental pollutant BDE-47 may impair male fertility by combining network toxicology, single-cell transcriptomics, and in vitro experiments. The authors identify Leydig cells as a key target and link BDE-47 exposure to downregulation of GSTM1 and molecular changes related to ferroptosis.

papers.title: Novel Hybrid Scaffold of Pyrazole, Thiazole, and [1,2,3]triazole: Eco-Friendly Synthesis by DABCO, Anti-HIV-1 RT, and In Silico Studies.
papers.abstract: The emergence of drug-resistant HIV-1 strains and limitations of current reverse transcriptase (RT) inhibitors support the development of structurally novel antiviral scaffolds. Hybrid azole systems may provide complementary interactions within the HIV-1 RT binding pocket.Purpose: To synthesize novel pyrazole-thiazole-[1,2,3]triazole hybrids using an eco-friendly DABCO-mediated approach and evaluate their anti-HIV-1 RT activity and structure-activity relationships using experimental and computational methods.
papers.summary: This paper reports an eco-friendly DABCO-mediated synthesis of novel hybrid compounds combining pyrazole, thiazole, and [1,2,3]triazole scaffolds, then tests them as inhibitors of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase. The authors combine experimental enzyme inhibition assays with in silico docking and structure-activity analysis to identify promising antiviral candidates.

papers.title: Experimental screening and structure-informed engineering of peptide-fused bacteriophage lysins with enhanced activity against Gram-negative bacteria.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria necessitates the development of novel antimicrobial strategies. Bacteriophage-derived lysins are promising options, but lysins against Gram-negative bacteria lose their activity under physiological conditions. Peptide fusion strategies have been used to address this problem with limited success. In this study, structure prediction and charge analysis were used to guide the selection of suitable peptides for engineering lysins against Gram-negative bacteria. Seven variants of LysPd138 were constructed by fusing it with different peptide
papers.summary: This study uses structure prediction and charge analysis to guide the design of peptide-fused variants of the bacteriophage lysin LysPd138, aiming to overcome the loss of activity against Gram-negative bacteria under physiological conditions. Seven variants were constructed and experimentally screened, demonstrating that structure-informed engineering can improve lysin activity. The work offers a rational design strategy for developing new antimicrobials against antibiotic-resistant Gram-negative pathogens.

papers.title: Identification of new fucosyltransferase-8 inhibitors: An integrated biochemical, biophysical, and computational approach.
papers.abstract: The α-1,6-fucosyltransferase (FUT8) mediated core fucosylation is responsible for several pathophysiological processes, including prostate cancer progression. FUT8 is a promising therapeutic target owing to its effects on cell migration and its capacity to convert androgen-dependent prostate cancer cells into androgen-independent cells. This study, therefore, investigates potential FUT8 inhibitors as therapeutic options for prostate cancer by targeting FUT8-mediated core fucosylation using in vitro, biophysical, and computational approaches. Eight of the 265 compounds showed significant cytoto
papers.summary: This study screened 265 compounds and identified eight that inhibit FUT8, the enzyme responsible for core fucosylation linked to prostate cancer progression. Using biochemical, biophysical, and computational methods, the authors characterized these inhibitors as potential therapeutic leads for prostate cancer. The work provides a starting point for developing drugs that target FUT8-mediated fucosylation.

papers.title: Network toxicology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations for bisphenol A neurotoxicity in depression pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA), a widespread environmental endocrine disruptor, can cross the blood-brain barrier and exert neurotoxic effects closely associated with depression pathogenesis. However, the precise molecular targets and signaling pathways mediating BPA-induced depression remain poorly understood. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, GEO transcriptomic dataset analysis, and in vivo experimental validation in mice to systematically investigate the potential toxicological targets and underlying mechanisms of BPA in depression. BPA-related t
papers.summary: This study combines network toxicology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and transcriptomic analysis with mouse experiments to identify molecular targets and pathways through which the environmental pollutant bisphenol A (BPA) may contribute to depression. The work proposes candidate toxicological targets linking BPA exposure to depressive pathology, offering mechanistic hypotheses for how this endocrine disruptor affects the brain.

papers.title: Experimental Study on Anxiolytic and Antidepressant Effects of Zhi-Chi-Jie-Yu Granules in CUMS Mice and Prediction of Underlying Molecular Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the in‑vivo pharmacological effects of Zhi-Chi-Jie-Yu Granules(ZCK) on CUMS‑induced anxiety‑ and depression‑like behaviors in mice. Post‑hoc exploratory analyses including network pharmacology and molecular docking were further performed to generate potential mechanistic hypotheses for its anti‑depressant action.
papers.summary: This study tested Zhi-Chi-Jie-Yu Granules (ZCK), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model and found that it reduced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. The authors then used network pharmacology and molecular docking to predict potential molecular targets and pathways underlying these effects. These mechanistic findings are exploratory hypotheses rather than experimentally validated mechanisms.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Antidepressant Mechanisms and Side Effects: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking Study of Amitriptyline, Mirtazapine, and Escitalopram for Treating Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.abstract: Amitriptyline, mirtazapine, and escitalopram are effective antidepressants for treating major depressive disorder (MDD). Our study aimed to use computational biology to understand the mechanisms for the similarities and differences in efficacies and side effects of these drugs.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular docking to compare how three antidepressants (amitriptyline, mirtazapine, and escitalopram) work at the molecular level and why they differ in efficacy and side effects. The computational approach identifies shared and distinct protein targets, offering mechanistic explanations for their clinical profiles in treating major depressive disorder.

papers.title: Monomeric CRP is prevalent in the blood of patients with rheumatoid arthritis and correlates with clinically relevant markers.
papers.abstract: Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) is a hallmark of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flares. CRP exists as pentameric (pCRP) and monomeric (mCRP) isoforms with distinct functions, with pCRP generally pro-inflammatory and mCRP more immunomodulatory. Standard clinical assays do not distinguish between these forms, and it remains unclear whether elevated CRP in RA reflects structural variation. We investigated CRP isoform distribution and function in RA using biomolecular and biophysical approaches.
papers.summary: This study examines whether the elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) seen in rheumatoid arthritis patients reflects different structural forms of the protein. Using biomolecular and biophysical methods, the authors find that monomeric CRP (mCRP) is prevalent in RA patient blood and correlates with clinically relevant disease markers, whereas standard clinical assays cannot distinguish between CRP isoforms. This suggests that isoform-specific CRP measurement could improve RA assessment.

papers.title: Integrating network analysis and machine learning to explore the pharmacological targets and associations of oleanolic acid in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), a major type of non-small cell lung cancer, has high incidence and mortality rates. Oleanolic acid (OA), a natural pentacyclic triterpene compound, has demonstrated potential anti-tumor effects but its pharmacological effects in LUAD remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study combines network analysis and machine learning to identify potential pharmacological targets of oleanolic acid in lung adenocarcinoma. The authors aim to clarify the anti-tumor mechanisms of this natural compound in LUAD, which are currently poorly understood.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening against multiple pockets of the monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK) to identify FDA-approved compounds that could be repurposed as antivirals. The approach targets an essential viral DNA replication enzyme, aiming to address the lack of effective targeted mpox therapies.

papers.title: Bioinspired and Biomimetic Nanocarriers: Advances in Exosomes and Cell-Membrane-Coated Systems for Therapeutic Applications.
papers.abstract: The translation of nanomedicine from bench to bedside has been thwarted by the limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles including rapid mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS) clearance, lack of target specificity, immunogenicity and poor intracellular delivery. To overcome these limitations, bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers are emerging as the next generation of therapeutic platforms. Bioinspired systems replicate the core biological design principles with engineered synthetic materials and biomimetic platforms use natural biological components such as cell membranes and extracel
papers.summary: This review discusses bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers, particularly exosomes and cell-membrane-coated systems, as next-generation therapeutic platforms that overcome limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles such as rapid immune clearance, poor targeting, and immunogenicity. It highlights how these systems replicate natural biological design principles to improve drug delivery and therapeutic efficacy.
